title: Autonomous warm-standby readiness fabric and multi-region failover orchestration
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement an autonomous "warm-standby readiness fabric" that keeps standby regions primed for immediate takeover while minimizing cost and avoiding noisy priming behavior. This ticket covers orchestration, health gating, model-variant compatibility checks, and integration points with routing and fallback policies.

Scope:
- Define readiness states (cold | primed | synced | hot) and transitions with clear SLOs for RTO and RPO.
- Implement multi-dimensional health probes (control-plane heartbeat, model variant compatibility check, KV cache priming score, sequence-length distribution check, and latency tail-checks).
- Build orchestration controller that will: 1) schedule priming work during low-cost windows, 2) run fast compatibility verification for fallback model variants, and 3) surface readiness level to smart-router.
- Add gating rules to smart routing: require synced KV cache OR model-variant fast-compat pass before region promoted to active for low-latency routes.
- Observability: per-region readiness metrics, priming throughput, priming error categories, and per-customer failover trace ID propagation.
- Rollout strategy: canary primary-to-standby failover simulation on non-prod regions, then incremental activation in a single customer pilot, then broad rollout.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Continuous full-KV priming vs. sampled prefix priming: choose sampled prefix + adaptive backfill to limit egress and token costs.
- Aggressive priming (always keep replica hot) increases cost; introduce dynamic budget and tier-aware priming where Tier-A customers keep longer warm windows than Tier-C.
- Compatibility check fast-path: run a trimmed-forward pass with 8-token prefixes against the requested model variant to verify kernel/path compatibility rather than full-length generation to save time.

Success criteria:
- Failover RTO < 6s for Tier-A flows in tests, < 20s for Tier-B flows.
- No >3x spike in cost for priming compared to baseline after rollout (expected ~1.2x with sampled priming).
- No customer-facing errors during automated failover drills in canary.

Related artifacts:
- Design spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RR/Warm+Standby+Readiness+Fabric
